findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify how DET triggers for T13/T14 are reconciled with ADR 0034's explicit decision to use LLM-routed (not lexical) applicability for these criteria, and confirm whether the triggers are route_criteria skip guards (LLM-tier skips) rather than DET-floor entries (which scan code, not plan prose).
evidence: ADR 0034 (docs/adr/0034-llm-routed-enumeration-overlays.md:35-37): 'Each is an exec:AGENT, overlay_routing:llm criterion... LLM-routed overlays are absent from the deterministic trigger map, so route_criteria never skips them'
ADR 0034: 'A lexical trigger over-fires on descriptive prose; an LLM-routed overlay running its own criterion call is more reliable'

ADR 0033 (docs/adr/0033-hedge-detector-1turn-not-det.md:13-16): 'The DET engine scans code, not plan prose. det_invariants.py engine_b.scan operates on code-file ASTs / file-glob patterns. A plan description is prose, not a code file'
696a comment (round 3): 'T13 71.0% fire (29% skip), T14 41.8% (58% skip) ... implement as _DET_OVERLAY_RULES entries'
findings.finding: The plan's 'DET triggers for zero-finding criteria' item proposes implementing T13 and T14 as `_DET_OVERLAY_RULES` entries (per the 696a evidence it cites). ADR 0034 explicitly decided the opposite: T13/T14 are `exec:AGENT, overlay_routing:llm` and are 'absent from the deterministic trigger map' because 'a lexical trigger over-fires on descriptive prose' — the LLM decides applicability. Adding DET regex triggers for T13/T14 would reverse a load-bearing ADR decision without stating a rationale for doing so; the DET engine also operates on code, not plan prose (ADR 0033 confirms this for the analogous hedge case), so a DET trigger scans the wrong artifact.
findings.location: Decomposition section — 'Independent stories/tasks: ... DET triggers for zero-finding criteria'; 696a evidence comment: 'implement as _DET_OVERLAY_RULES entries'
scenarios: A DET regex trigger for T13 that scans the plan description for prohibition language would fire on plans that describe (but don't introduce) a prohibition — the same false-positive problem ADR 0034 rejected.

A regex that misses plans using synonyms or indirect language for prohibitions would silently skip T13 — a silent never-evaluate failure mode the plan itself identifies as 'the failure mode' to avoid.

The DET engine's code-file scan infrastructure has no path to apply a criterion to plan prose, so the 'DET trigger' would need to be implemented as a pre-LLM skip rule in the LLM tier (route_criteria), not in det_floor — a different mechanism than the plan implies.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename this work item to 'route_criteria skip guards for zero-finding criteria' and restrict DET/lexical triggers to the criteria whose zero-finding rate is driven by plan-prose patterns the LLM tier already decides (T13/T14 stay LLM-routed per ADR 0034; the asserted-capability and removal-rationale triggers that fire on module-ref+capability-verb conjunctions are reasonable candidates for route_criteria pre-screening rather than full DET-floor entries).

findings.finding: Child bfa8 adds the T10 DET overlay rule to registry.py as a plain regex string ('Add the audited T10 regex... to the deterministic overlay rules in registry.py'), but child 4ee2 — which must land before bfa8 per the parent's criteria_routing.json chain ordering — migrates the entire _DET_OVERLAY_RULES table from plain regex strings to DetGateRule objects, covering only T5a/T5d/T7/T12. After 4ee2 lands, the table is DetGateRule-typed; bfa8 must then add T10 as a DetGateRule, not a plain string, but bfa8's approach and scope make no mention of DetGateRule and present the addition as a plain-regex operation. This is a conflicting assumption about the table's format at the time bfa8 runs.
scenarios: Developer implements bfa8 after 4ee2 has landed and adds T10 as a plain string to a DetGateRule-typed dict — Python type error or silent behavioral failure when overlay_triggers tries to evaluate it as a DetGateRule

Developer implements bfa8 before 4ee2 (to avoid the conflict), adding T10 as a plain string — then 4ee2 migrates only T5a/T5d/T7/T12 and leaves T10 as a plain string in a mixed-type table, causing overlay_triggers to fail for T10
4ee2's behavior-preservation test for 'existing entries' only covers T5a/T5d/T7/T12 and would not catch a malformed T10 entry added by bfa8

Update bfa8's AC to include a test that the T10 entry is a DetGateRule instance and fires identically to the audited regex on representative texts.

findings.finding: The Decomposition names 'optional genai-prices costing' as an independent story/child ticket, but AC1 mandates 'Every child ticket below is closed.' An item marked optional may legitimately remain open, making AC1 either self-contradicting (it can never pass if the optional child is skipped) or silently untestable (the checker must know to exclude it, but no exclusion is stated).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC1 vs. Decomposition 'optional genai-prices costing'
